brief: A Market Ear chart compilation on the session's extreme de-risking. GS's vol desk flagged VIX spot above 28, its highest close since March, with VIX sitting about 4 vol points above the UX1 future, the most inverted term structure since April 2025. GS's trading desk said ES1 top-of-book depth averaged just $4.2m, one of the worst liquidity sessions in four years, which it says exacerbates price moves. GS Prime charts show the breadth of de-risking exceeding the 'Lib Lows' and the 2022 meltdown, with a spike in single-stock selling that began before this week. Per MS PB data, US long/short hedge fund net exposure fell to 42%, a one-year low and the 8th percentile since 2010. At comparable past levels, median forecast S&P 500 NTM earnings growth has been 5%, versus a 16% consensus for next year, and never above 10% historically. MS QDS estimates systematic strategies have $25bn left to sell over the next week, though leverage entered the session at only the 25th percentile. GS Prime says three years of momentum exposure building has been erased in under three months, and ICI data shows mutual funds hold little cash to buy any dip.
